title: Why Do Your Ears RUMBLE When You Yawn? 👂
description:
Yawn. A big one. Hear that low rumble in your ears? That's a muscle flexing: a tiny one in your middle ear (the tensor tympani) that tugs on the hammer bone and pulls your eardrum in tight, like tuning a drum skin. A tight eardrum passes less low sound, which is why everything goes a little muffled. Its everyday job is turning down loud noises you make yourself, like your own chewing. Up to half of people say they can rumble it on purpose, no yawn needed (that's from a survey, so the real share may be lower). Researchers at the University of Bath are now testing an ear camera that watches the eardrum move, so people who can barely move could type with a rumble. Could you do it without yawning? Yes or no?
